name: Winston Churchill
achievements: Prime Minister of the United Kingdom 1940–1945 | Prime Minister of the United Kingdom 1951–1955 | Nobel Prize in Literature 1953
relations: father:Lord Randolph Churchill | mother:Jennie Jerome | spouse:Clementine Hozier (married 1908)
notes: Led Britain through most of the Second World War.

name: Julius Caesar
achievements: Conquered Gaul 58–50 BC | Crossed the Rubicon 49 BC, starting a civil war | Introduced the Julian calendar 46 BC | Wrote the Commentarii on the Gallic and Civil Wars
relations: ally:Pompey | ally:Crassus | heir:Octavian | partner:Cleopatra | spouse:Calpurnia | daughter:Julia | assassin:Marcus Junius Brutus | ally:Mark Antony
notes: Made dictator for life in 44 BC and assassinated weeks later in the Senate.

name: Clement of Rome
achievements: Traditionally the author of First Clement, the church at Rome's letter to Corinth
notes: Flourished late in the 1st century; listed by early writers as the third or fourth bishop of Rome.

name: Adolf Hitler
notes: Leader of Nazi Germany; his invasion of Poland began the war in Europe.

name: Franklin D. Roosevelt
achievements: President of the United States 1933–1945 | The New Deal | Lend-Lease
notes: Led the USA into the war after Pearl Harbor; died weeks before victory in Europe.

name: Joseph Stalin
achievements: Leader of the Soviet Union c. 1924–1953
notes: Signed the 1939 pact with Hitler, then led the USSR against Germany after 1941.

name: Harry S. Truman
notes: Became President on Roosevelt's death and ordered the atomic bombings of Japan.

name: Dwight D. Eisenhower
achievements: Supreme Allied Commander in Europe 1943–1945 | President of the United States 1953–1961
notes: Commanded the D-Day landings and the Allied advance into Germany.

name: Bernard Montgomery
aliases: Field Marshal Viscount Montgomery of Alamein | Monty
achievements: Commanded the Eighth Army at El Alamein 1942 | Commanded Allied ground forces on D-Day 1944
notes: British commander in North Africa, Italy and north-west Europe.

name: Ptolemy II Philadelphus
achievements: King of Ptolemaic Egypt 283–246 BCE, co-regent with his father from 285/284 BCE | Expanded the Library and Mouseion of Alexandria | The Pharos lighthouse of Alexandria completed in his reign
relations: father:Ptolemy I Soter | mother:Berenice I | spouse:Arsinoe II, his sister (hence "Philadelphus", sibling-loving)
notes: The Letter of Aristeas (WR-0002) credits him with commissioning the Greek translation of the Torah, the Septuagint: a tradition, not established fact.
